Instrument (EN): Chinese Symptom Catastrophizing Scale — 12-item adaptation for cardiac surgery patients
Scales / measured domains (EN): Three factor scores: Helplessness (5 items), Magnification (4), Rumination (3); composite 0–48 from twelve 0–4 rated items; no clinically validated automated risk cutoff.
Research provenance: Duo Zhang et al. Health Psychology and Behavioral Medicine, published 2026-10-10; DOI 10.1080/21642850.2026.2744739. Translated original 13-item English Post-concussion Symptom Catastrophizing Scale (PCS-CS); two overlapping original helplessness items were combined, making a distinct 12-item Chinese adaptation. Convenience N676 Chinese cardiac surgery patients recruited June–Oct 2025, internal split EFA N338 and CFA N338 (not two independent populations); total alpha .936, CFI .970, RMSEA .059, ICC .958 in small retest subsample.
DB locales: No published Holistic House assessment version. Research ZH-CN only. Not identical to existing generic Pain Catastrophizing Scale PCS-13 or 13-item PCS-CS.
EN form: Parent English PCS-CS uses 13 items; an independently validated EN twelve-item version is NOT shown.
RU form: No Russian respondent adaptation validated in this 2026 source.
ES form: No Spanish respondent adaptation validated in this 2026 source.
Other translations: ZH-CN: Chinese culturally adapted 12-item respondent form studied in perioperative Chinese cardiac surgery patients (N676); this is a measured adaptation, not general-population Chinese norms.
Target population: Adults undergoing cardiac surgery at two hospital centers in China, convenience sample N676; neither unselected community respondents nor post-concussion populations nor clinical thresholds studied.

Instrument (EN): Trauma-Informed Climate Scale–10 — Turkish healthcare professional adaptation
Scales / measured domains (EN): One measured domain: staff-rated trauma-informed organizational/service climate, ten items; Turkish unidimensional form (PCA explained 50.52%); no independent PTSD/trauma symptom screening subscales.
Research provenance: Tuğba Yılmaz, Yusuf Ziya Koç, Eda Şen, Rüşen Sinecem. Current Approaches in Psychiatry, early online 2026-10-04; DOI 10.18863/pgy.1958518. Translation, back translation, expert review; cross-sectional N410 healthcare professionals at Turkish institutions, test/retest n49. One factor, alpha=omega=lambda .89, CFA CFI .915, TLI .89, SRMR .056, ICC .72 (95% CI .20–.89). One study, not an independent replication.
DB locales: No live Holistic House assessment edition. Turkish study TR-TR not currently public on site or in database.
EN form: Original Hales et al. (2019) English TICS-10 exists, but the Turkish paper is NOT a new independently validated EN translation.

Target population: Turkish healthcare professionals employed in healthcare organizations, N410; respondents evaluate workplace care climate, not their own PTSD symptoms.
